summary: MARS is an educational simulation developed by Team ElektroLab for children aged 7–12. Built with Godot, it places players in charge of a scientific base in Deuteronilus Mensae, Mars. Before starting, players configure the available power systems and choose their astronaut and rover teams. During a six-sol mission, they manage four interconnected panels: Energy, Life Support, Lab, and Operations. Rovers collect raw scientific data, while astronauts or automated equipment process it to advance toward a 150 GB objective. Players must also manage batteries, oxygen, water, crew energy, maintenance, and equipment failures. The experience introduces electronics and electrical engineering concepts through interactive decisions and simplified mathematical models.
details:
Project Overview

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational simulation game developed by Team ElektroLab for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It introduces children aged 7–12 to electronics, electricity, engineering, and the challenges of managing a scientific base on Mars.

How It Works

Developed using Godot 4 and GDScript, the game places players in charge of a simulated base in Deuteronilus Mensae, Mars.

Before starting, players configure their mission by selecting photovoltaic and wind power systems alongside mandatory nuclear fission and battery storage. They also choose between two and five astronauts and one to three rovers.

During a six-sol mission, players manage four interconnected modules:

  • Energy: Electrical generation, battery storage, power consumption, and equipment failures.
  • Life Support: Oxygen, water, temperature, and system maintenance.
  • Lab: Scientific data processing and rover repairs using human or automated systems.
  • Operations: Astronaut assignments, rest, rover exploration, charging, and maintenance.

Rovers collect raw data from the Martian surface, while astronauts or automated laboratory equipment process it. Automated systems work faster but consume more electrical power.

The objective is to process 150 GB of scientific data while maintaining the base's essential systems.

Innovation and Educational Impact

The game uses simplified mathematical models to connect electrical generation, power demand, resource consumption, equipment reliability, and scientific productivity.

Children learn that engineering involves making decisions, balancing resources, and understanding how one system affects another.

The project combines interactive gameplay, scientific concepts, and engineering-based problem-solving to make space exploration more accessible to young learners.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed using Godot 4, GDScript, scene-based interfaces, mathematical simulation models, and AI-assisted development tools.

Scientific concepts were informed by NASA resources. Numerical gameplay parameters are educational approximations rather than validated specifications of a real Martian base.
